transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-18
Start time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Elena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Rachel Singh (CTO - Carepoint), Derek Coleman (Head of ML), Ana Torres (Compliance), Samir Patel (PM)

---- Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect) ----
Redwood and Carepoint align on POC goals: measure quality on patient-facing prompts, evaluate hallucination rates, enforce output format constraints for patient-safety, and run latency/cost benchmarks across hosted and dedicated options.

00:00 Elena Park: "Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll kick off. I'm Elena from Redwood, along with Marcus on the SE side. Can you folks quickly intro?"
00:12 Rachel Singh: "Rachel, CTO at Carepoint — we own the patient assistant roadmap. Goal is to reduce triage time and improve patient messaging accuracy."
00:22 Derek Coleman: "Derek, head of ML. We're looking at model safety, hallucination metrics, and how to integrate with our PHI filters."
00:32 Ana Torres: "Ana, compliance. I'll be driving SOC2, data residency, and encryption questions."
00:42 Marcus Lee: "Great, quick agenda: success criteria + workload sizing, then the quality eval plan — golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination checks, and scoring. Then timelines and next steps."
01:05 Samir Patel: "And we'll want to see how this affects latency and cost — especially on peak times in clinics."
01:18 Elena Park: "Perfect. First, success criteria. Rachel, what would success look like from Carepoint's perspective?"
01:28 Rachel Singh: "We want at least 90% acceptable responses on a blinded human eval for patient-facing prompts, less than 2% critical hallucinations for medication/dosage content, and end-to-end latency under 600ms on typical queries. Also a clear path to private deployment if needed."
01:46 Marcus Lee: "90% human acceptability, <2% critical hallucinations, and <600ms — got it. We'll parse that into the scoring rubric."
01:55 Derek Coleman: "On the hallucination spec: we'll need to define 'critical' vs 'non-critical'. Critical = anything that asserts a medication, dosage, or instruction. Non-critical is generic hallucination about non-clinical facts."
02:10 Ana Torres: "Also, for compliance, any PII/PHI leakage tests must be explicit — are you storing prompts? retention?"
02:20 Elena Park: "We will share our retention docs — Redwood hosted by default does ephemeral request logs for trial, and dedicated/private has configurable retention and KMS options. We'll attach the SOC2 summary after this call."
02:38 Marcus Lee: "Okay, moving into workload sizing. Samir, can you describe expected QPS and token mix?"
02:47 Samir Patel: "Baseline is 30 QPS during peak for our U.S. clinics, average query length ~25 tokens user + expected 80 tokens model output. Burst to 80 QPS for brief periods."
03:02 Marcus Lee: "So roughly 30-80 QPS, token budget ~105 tokens per request. For 8-hour clinical day, that's about X tokens — we'll run numbers in the follow-up benchmark doc."
03:16 Rachel Singh: "One thing: some prompts will be multimodal later, but not in this POC — text only for now."
03:24 Marcus Lee: "Noted. Now the quality eval plan: we'll build a golden prompt set, regression tests, hallucination checks, format validators, and scoring. Marcus: can you outline the golden prompt process?"
03:34 Marcus Lee: "Sure — we ask Carepoint to provide 50-100 representative prompts across categories: triage, scheduling, med-info, follow-ups. We'll redact any PHI. Redwood will augment with paraphrases to create ~500 test cases. For each prompt we create a golden reference answer or set of acceptable outputs; human raters will annotate and we will run automatic regex/format checks for structured outputs (e.g., JSON with keys)."
03:58 Derek Coleman: "On paraphrases — please ensure semantic equivalence, not changing the intent. Also we'll flag prompts that require deterministic outputs vs. open-ended."
04:10 Marcus Lee: "Good point. We'll mark each test case as deterministic, constrained, or open-ended. Deterministic will require exact or format match, constrained will use a set of acceptable answers, and open-ended will use human scoring."
04:22 Samir Patel: "What about hallucination checks?"
04:25 Marcus Lee: "We'll include targeted hallucination probes: fact-check tests for medications, dosages, contraindications. Those have binary pass/fail and escalate to 'critical' if they return unsafe assertions."
04:37 Ana Torres: "How will you simulate PHI scenarios? We can't send real PHI to hosted endpoints in the trial."
04:45 Elena Park: "We recommend synthetic PHI or placeholders (e.g., [PATIENT_1]). For security review, Redwood can run the eval in a customer-dedicated VPC or on-prem if required; for initial smoke tests we'll use redacted data on hosted."
04:59 Rachel Singh: "OK we will provide redacted examples."
05:04 Marcus Lee: "Scoring approach: a combined metric — weighted score = 0.5 * human_acceptability + 0.3 * hallucination_penalty + 0.2 * format/completeness. Human acceptability is mean over blind raters (0-1), hallucination penalty subtracts for critical failures, format/completeness is fraction passing schema validators."
05:33 Derek Coleman: "Can we see the scoring formula numerically? Example: if human_accept 0.92, critical hallucinations 0.03, format pass 0.95, how would that score?"
05:44 Marcus Lee: "Example: weighted = 0.5*0.92 + 0.3*(1 - critical_rate) + 0.2*0.95 = 0.46 + 0.3*0.97 + 0.19 = 0.46 + 0.291 + 0.19 = 0.941. We can provide a spreadsheet with the calc and thresholds for go/no-go."
06:10 Samir Patel: "That's helpful. For regression tests, how are you keeping baselines?"
06:14 Marcus Lee: "We snapshot a baseline model variant at POC start — we'll store model hash/version, config (temperature, max tokens, quantization), and run nightly regression for the test set. Any drop beyond configured delta triggers an alert and we run root-cause."
06:31 Elena Park: "We support model pinning so you can roll forward in a controlled way. For Dedicated you'll have the option to host a pinned version on reserved capacity."
06:43 Rachel Singh: "What about automated format checks? We have strict JSON schema for downstream ingestion."
06:48 Marcus Lee: "We'll implement JSON schema validation in the eval harness; outputs failing schema will be marked as format fails and counted in the 0.2 component of the score. We'll also do fuzzy matching for enumerated fields."
07:05 Derek Coleman: "How do you measure hallucination rate? Is it purely human-annotated?"
07:10 Marcus Lee: "A mix: targeted probes flagged for automated fact-checking against our knowledge base where possible, plus human annotation for edge cases. For medication facts we'll validate against a vetted med table. If automated check is inconclusive, it goes to human raters."
07:27 Ana Torres: "Raters — where are they located? Are they HIPAA trained?"
07:31 Elena Park: "Redwood uses a vetted rater provider for these experiments; for anything with PHI or sensitive data we can route reviews to the customer's team or use a secure review process. We'll clarify in the SOC2 docs."
07:45 Samir Patel: "Timelines?"
07:47 Marcus Lee: "Proposed timeline: Carepoint provides prompt set and success criteria by 2026-02-22. Redwood builds eval harness and golden prompts augmented set by 2026-02-25. Redwood runs baseline benchmarks across hosted model variants (latency/cost) by 2026-02-27. We share results and schedule follow-up demo week of 2026-03-02."
08:09 Rachel Singh: "That timeline works for us, pending internal approvals. We'll try to accelerate the prompt delivery."
08:17 Elena Park: "On benchmarking — we'll do 3 model variants: small quantized (cost-focused), mid variant (balanced), and high-quality variant. We'll report latency p50/p90/p99, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens."
08:33 Derek Coleman: "Do you include KV cache / prefix caching in those numbers? Because our flows often have long conversation context."
08:39 Marcus Lee: "Yes we'll include representative chat traces including KV cache warm vs cold — though initial numbers will be cold start, we'll add warm-run numbers in the follow-up."
08:52 Samir Patel: "Any limits on the eval harness? e.g., concurrency for load tests?"
08:57 Marcus Lee: "We can simulate the 30-80 QPS bursts you mentioned. For hosted trials we might have rate limits; we'll coordinate with infra to provision temporary burst capacity for the smoke runs."
09:10 Ana Torres: "Security doc ask: we need KMS details, audit logs, SSO/SAML, RBAC, and data residency options."
09:18 Elena Park: "We'll send the security package and SOC2 summary. For Dedicated/Private we'll outline the KMS integrations and HSM options."
09:26 Rachel Singh: "One compliance question: are request logs ever used for model training?"
09:31 Elena Park: "By default no for enterprise customers — Redwood does not use customer request data to train public models; we can sign that in the contract, and for hosted trials we can enable a no-training flag and ephemeral retention."
09:44 Derek Coleman: "Good. About evaluation infrastructure — do you provide the harness as code (github) so we can run internally?"
09:50 Marcus Lee: "Yes we can provide the eval harness as a repo with scripts. For private deployments we can run it in your environment, or we can run it in Redwood's secure infra and share results — whichever you prefer."
10:05 Samir Patel: "We prefer to run locally for PHI tests. We'll need a clean docker image and instructions."
10:12 Marcus Lee: "We'll package that. Now, edge cases: for structured outputs where the assistant must return appointment suggestions, we will require exact JSON keys and value types — those will be in the deterministic bucket."
10:28 Rachel Singh: "Also want to measure hallucination severity — ranking from 1-5 maybe — critical if 4-5."
10:35 Marcus Lee: "We can map severity into the scoring: any severity 4-5 reduces the '1 - critical_rate' term significantly; we'll show examples in the rubric."
10:48 Derek Coleman: "About human raters: what's the inter-rater agreement threshold?"
10:52 Marcus Lee: "We target Krippendorff's alpha > 0.6 for the subjective items; if below we'll rework the rubric and retrain raters."
11:03 Ana Torres: "Audit trail for evals — we need immutable logs for any PII-handling runs."
11:09 Elena Park: "We can provide audit logs export, and for Private deployments logs remain in your VPC with customer-managed KMS."
11:18 Rachel Singh: "Costs — show us the per-token cost delta between small quantized and high-quality variant."
11:24 Marcus Lee: "We'll include cost per 1k tokens and estimated monthly cost at your projected QPS. Also show cost savings from batching and prefix caching."
11:35 Samir Patel: "On batching: what's the latency tradeoff?"
11:38 Marcus Lee: "We can tune batching windows; small batch windows keep p50 latency low while saving tokens. We'll show suggested configs that meet your 600ms goal."
11:48 Derek Coleman: "Are there any red flags for private deployment? e.g., on-prem GPU availability or model size constraints?"
11:54 Marcus Lee: "For on-prem we recommend nodes with x GPUs depending on throughput; if you need large LLMs we can provide quantized variants to reduce memory. We'll produce a capacity planning sheet with GPU counts and expected throughput."
12:08 Elena Park: "Okay let's recap next steps."
12:11 Elena Park: "Marcus — deliver golden prompt set + harness by 2026-02-25. Elena — send security and pricing docs by 2026-02-20. Carepoint (Rachel) — provide prompts and success criteria by 2026-02-22. Ana — confirm compliance items by 2026-02-24. We'll run baseline by 2026-02-27 and meet week of 2026-03-02."
12:38 Rachel Singh: "Sounds good. Thanks everyone."
12:41 Elena Park: "Thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invite for the results review and attach the harness link."

---- End transcript ----

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription had occasional mis-hearings of technical terms (e.g., KV cache transcribed as K V cash), and product names like "Redwood Dedicated" may appear as "Redwood dedicate". Speaker overlaps are possible in a few short segments.
